items.title: Plas Johnson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996
items.q: And when I talk to players, like Ricky, you know Ricky is a player that came up the same way and we were talking about that last night.

ctx.x: It’s a revelation to me, but that’s not what the book is, the book is about licks. I’m self taught and when I think back over it my first experience with playing when I didn’t know how to play or what to play was listening to other players play and copying, copying what they play or trying to mimic what they play. And it does turn out to be licks, like a study of blues playing, it’s like licks. You can’t say well it’s just three chord changes. You know better. It’s licks, a little two-bar, one-bar, four-bar…
Usually there’s one or two people that will speak to you I think, you know?
